I'll explore the DingoDB workspace structure and key docs so I can give you a clear read on what the project is.Reading the main docs to form a coherent picture of architecture and intent.## Yes — I understand the project

**DingoDB** is currently a **specification-only** repo (MIT license). There is no application source, build system, or tests yet — only design docs (~5.6k lines) that define a new kind of database.

### One-line pitch

> **Damage the database. Keep the data you did not destroy.**

A damage-tolerant, high-performance store for arbitrary digital material: records, logs, documents, blobs, unknown formats, even uninterpreted bytes.

### Core idea

Most DBs fail as one object: corrupt a catalog/engine/file and healthy bytes become unreachable. DingoDB treats storage as a **fabric of independently survivable data islands**:

- Frames, chunks, and segments are independently framed and verified  
- A hole in the middle does **not** poison data after it  
- Catalogs/indexes are **derived** and rebuildable — not the only map back to the bytes  
- Recovery rule: *what is gone is gone; what remains still lives*  
- Physical survival ≠ semantic completeness (surviving events after a hole stay valid; state that needs missing history is incomplete/uncertain)

### Four promises

| Promise | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Independent survival** | Localized damage → localized loss; salvage scans surviving islands |
| **Extreme speed** | Append-oriented ingestion, hot in-memory indexes; Redis-class hot path with explicit durability modes |
| **Massive retention** | One logical store across memory → disk → object store → archive; movable self-describing segments |
| **SDA examination** | Structured Data Algebra for deterministic inspect/transform of recovered data *and* holes |

payload.text:
I'll explore the DingoDB workspace structure and key docs so I can give you a clear read on what the project is.Reading the main docs to form a coherent picture of architecture and intent.## Yes — I understand the project

**DingoDB** is currently a **specification-only** repo (MIT license). There is no application source, build system, or tests yet — only design docs (~5.6k lines) that define a new kind of database.

### One-line pitch

> **Damage the database. Keep the data you did not destroy.**

A damage-tolerant, high-performance store for arbitrary digital material: records, logs, documents, blobs, unknown formats, even uninterpreted bytes.

### Core idea

Most DBs fail as one object: corrupt a catalog/engine/file and healthy bytes become unreachable. DingoDB treats storage as a **fabric of independently survivable data islands**:

- Frames, chunks, and segments are independently framed and verified  
- A hole in the middle does **not** poison data after it  
- Catalogs/indexes are **derived** and rebuildable — not the only map back to the bytes  
- Recovery rule: *what is gone is gone; what remains still lives*  
- Physical survival ≠ semantic completeness (surviving events after a hole stay valid; state that needs missing history is incomplete/uncertain)

### Four promises

| Promise | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| **Independent survival** | Localized damage → localized loss; salvage scans surviving islands |
| **Extreme speed** | Append-oriented ingestion, hot in-memory indexes; Redis-class hot path with explicit durability modes |
| **Massive retention** | One logical store across memory → disk → object store → archive; movable self-describing segments |
| **SDA examination** | Structured Data Algebra for deterministic inspect/transform of recovered data *and* holes |

### Spec map

| Doc | Role |
|-----|------|
| `README.md` | Product intro + status |
| `USP.md` | Product thesis / why it exists |
| `OVERVIEW.md` | Normative architecture (invariants, model, recovery, performance) |
| `FORMAT_SPEC.md` | Wire/survival format: frames, segments, salvage scanner |
| `SDA_SPEC.md` | Core SDA algebra (Seq/Set/Bag/Map, eliminators, comprehensions) |
| `SDA_PROFILE.md` | DingoDB-specific recovery examination units (holes, integrity, uncertainty) |
| `CLUSTER_SPEC.md` | Federation of recoverable partitions; partition-local consensus; control plane ≠ payload authority |
| `DX_SPEC.md` | Everyday DX: embedded/server/cluster, collection API, CLI doctor/salvage, progressive disclosure |

### Everyday product shape (when built)

Familiar collection API (`put` / `get` / `find`), schemaless JSON + bytes first-class, same logical model for embedded → server → cluster. Power (SDA, durability modes, salvage) is progressive disclosure. MVP aims at zero-config embedded, one solid SDK, resyncable journal, immutable segments, island recovery, doctor/salvage CLI, and corruption/perf tests.

### Status / repo state

- **Phase:** specification (Draft v0.1)  
- **Code:** none  
- **Git:** few “init” commits on `main`; working tree has only `.gremlin` / `.tinker` untracked tooling dirs  

### Mental model I will use going forward

DingoDB ≈ **append-only survival fabric** + **rebuildable accelerators** + **honest recovery evidence** + **SDA as the long-term examination language** — not SQL-by-default, not “magic undelete,” and not global coordination on the hot path.

---

**What I changed:** nothing — this was a read-only orientation pass over the docs and repo layout.

payload.summary:
I'll look through the workspace for the existing SDA and any related design docs so we can stage a delivery plan from what's already written.Reading the overview and specs to map scope, dependencies, and a sensible staged delivery plan.Drafting a staged delivery plan grounded in the specs and README initial target, with clear exit criteria per stage.## Summary

Added a staged delivery plan grounded in the existing specs (SDA already written; codebase later).

### Created: [`DELIVERY_PLAN.md`](DELIVERY_PLAN.md)

**10 stages**, each with deliverables, exit criteria, and normative spec anchors:

| Stage | Focus |
|-------|--------|
| **0** | Repo/CI harness when code lands |
| **1** | **SDA standalone** (pure, §14 conformance) — first product code |
| **2** | Wire format + salvage scanner (damage early) |
| **3** | Single-node append store + durability modes |
| **4** | Embedded collection SDK (ordinary put/get/filter DX) |
| **5** | SDA examination profile over recovered units/holes |
| **6** | Indexes, catalogs, history, chunked payloads |
| **7** | CLI doctor/salvage + server (completes README initial target) |
| **8** | Cluster (only after single-node salvage is real) |
| **9** | Tiering / long retention |

Also includes:

- Delivery principles (spec-first, vertical slices, conformance gates)
- Spec → stage map
- Parallelism rules (what can fan out after Stage 1)
- Quality bars and freeze points
- Demo milestones (“algebra works” → “punch a hole” → “database that survives” …)
- Open decisions deferred until the codebase arrives

### Updated: [`README.md`](README.md)

Linked the plan from the Status section.

### Sequencing rationale

SDA ships first because it is already fully specified and has no storage dependency. Survival framing and salvage land **before** a polished KV API so independent islands are not bolted on later. Cluster and archive tiers wait until single-node recovery is proven.
